subject: Recap: leadership alignment and procurement path for Novaterra
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.inference.com>
To: Claire Hughes <claire.hughes@novaterra.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.inference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: leadership alignment and procurement path for Novaterra

Hi Claire —

Thanks again for your time today. Wanted to capture a concise recap and proposed next steps so leadership and procurement have a single source of truth. Please flag anything I missed.

Key business outcomes you confirmed
- Reduce inference spend on customer-facing features by ~40% while meeting a 75th percentile latency target of <120ms.
- Move from PoC to pilot with 3 product teams (Search, Recommendations, Support) in Q2.
- Maintain data residency in us-west and enable audit logs for regulatory reporting.

Primary risks / blockers you raised
- Procurement needs a fixed-monthly commitment or clear overage policy.
- Security team requires SOC 2 Type II evidence + architecture diagram and encryption details.
- Lead engineer highlighted concern about tokenization differences and output parity vs current hosted model.

Immediate asks / owner
1) Procurement review: Claire to introduce Evan Park (procurement) and confirm budget cadence — owner: Claire — eta: Wed 3/24.
2) Security packet: Redwood to send SOC 2 summary, KMS integration notes, and a brief runbook — owner: Redwood (Vanessa) — eta: Thu 3/25. Attachment: Novaterra_Security_QA_responses_20270323.pdf (stub).
3) Pilot SOW and cost profile: Redwood to propose a 3-month pilot SOW with committed capacity and example cost comparisons (on-demand vs reserved) — owner: Redwood (Ben) — eta: Mon 3/29. Attachment: Novaterra_MVP_scope_20270322.pdf (stub).
4) Technical deep-dive: schedule with lead engineer to validate output parity and sample tokens — owner: Claire + Redwood tech lead — eta: next week.

Proposed procurement path (recommended)
- Initial pilot: 3-month reserved capacity with capped overage rate; monthly checkpoints and one executive review at pilot midpoint.
- If pilot meets latency and cost targets, convert to annual reserved capacity with standard enterprise SLA.

I'll follow up with attachments and a calendar invite for the technical deep-dive once Evan is on the thread.

Thanks,

Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.inference.com

Thanks Stephanie — clear and helpful. I agree with the outcomes and the suggested path. A few clarifications from my side:

- Procurement cadence: we run monthly vendor reviews but need a committed spend figure for the CFO to approve a pilot with reserved capacity. Evan, looping you in to confirm what documentation you need to evaluate the pilot commitment.
- Security: our InfoSec will prioritize SOC 2 artifacts and a short architecture diagram (network flow, KMS, logging).
- Pilot scope: can you include an example of expected monthly token throughput per product team (Search/Recommendations/Support) + expected cost delta vs our current provider? That will make the CFO ask concrete.

Cc'ing Evan so he can advise on procurement timeline. I can also book a 30-minute technical sync for Thurs/Friday next week if that works.

Claire Hughes
VP Product, Novaterra

Claire / team — I have a draft SOW and two cost scenarios attached: (1) pilot reserved capacity with capped overage, (2) on-demand trial with higher unit costs. Summary below:

Pilot reserved (recommended)
- 3-month pilot, committed GPU-hours aligned to expected token throughput of ~120M tokens/month across teams.
- Monthly commit: $45k/mo with 10% capped overage.
- Executive checkpoint at 6 weeks to validate latency and cost metrics.

On-demand trial
- No commit, pay-as-you-go. Cost estimate: ~25% higher per token for the same throughput.
- Lower procurement friction but less predictable budgeting.

I'll attach the SOW and a short cost-per-team breakdown. If procurement needs a lower initial commit, we can propose a stepped commit (month 1 lower, ramp to full commit month 2).

Attachments: Novaterra_SOW_draft_v1.docx, Novaterra_MVP_scope_20270322.pdf

Next steps:
- Evan, can you confirm whether a stepped commit would be acceptable to finance, or whether they need a firm monthly number?
- Claire, after Evan confirms, I'll finalize the SOW and share a DocuSign-ready file.

Thanks — Ben
